plan.hypothesis: H0: all group means are equal; H1: at least one group mean differs (population η² = 0.08)
assumptions: Fixed effects one-way ANOVA with 3 independent groups
Balanced design: 25 participants per group
Observations are independent normal random variables
Common variance across all groups (homogeneity of variance)
Population η² = 0.08 defines the non-centrality structure
Omnibus F-test at two-tailed α = 0.05
scientific_notes: Omnibus F-test: H0 states all group means equal; H1 at least one differs
Effect size quantified by η² = Var(group means) / σ²_pooled; related to f = √(η²/(1-η²))
With η² = 0.08, the ANOVA effect size f ≈ 0.294
Power computed using non-central F distribution with (k-1, N-k) df and non-centrality λ = f√N
Balanced allocation ensures maximum power under equal variances
Output metric: power at fixed sample size and significance level

answer.summary: Power for the omnibus F-test in a balanced one-way ANOVA with 3 independent groups, total sample size 75 (25 per group), population eta-squared 0.08, and significance level alpha = 0.05 is 0.269 (probability).
answer.method: Analytic calculation using non-central F-distribution: (1) convert population eta-squared (η² = 0.08) to Cohen's ANOVA effect size f = √[η²/(1−η²)] ≈ 0.295; (2) compute non-centrality parameter λ = f√N ≈ 2.554; (3) find critical F-value F_crit(2, 72; α=0.05) ≈ 3.124; (4) evaluate power = Pr(F > F_crit | λ) using the non-central F distribution with numerator df = 2 and denominator df = 72.
assumptions: Fixed effects one-way ANOVA with k = 3 independent groups
Balanced design with n = 25 participants per group
Total sample size N = 75
Observations are independent and normally distributed within each group
Common variance across all groups (homogeneity of variance assumption)
Population effect size quantified by η² = 0.08
Two-tailed omnibus F-test at significance level α = 0.05
Null hypothesis: H₀ all group means are equal; Alternative: H₁ at least one group mean differs
limitations: This is a fixed sample size power calculation; it does not account for potential violations of normality or equality of variance assumptions in practice
Power is modest (~27%) at the specified design and effect size; larger sample size or stronger effect would increase power
The calculation assumes the population effect size is exactly η² = 0.08; variation in true effect size would change actual power
No correction for multiple comparisons beyond the omnibus test is included

# Balanced one-way ANOVA power calculation
# Design: 3 independent groups, total N = 75, balanced
# Effect size: population eta-squared = 0.08
# Significance level: alpha = 0.05

# Parameters
k <- 3  # number of groups
N <- 75  # total sample size
n_per_group <- N / k  # balanced allocation
eta_sq <- 0.08  # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level

# Verify balanced design
cat("Study Design:\n")
cat("Number of groups (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Total sample size (N):", N, "\n")
cat("Per-group sample size (n):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio: 1:1:1 (balanced)\n")
cat("Population eta-squared (η²):", eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n\n")

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f (ANOVA effect size)
# f = sqrt(η² / (1 - η²))
f <- sqrt(eta_sq / (1 - eta_sq))
cat("Converted to ANOVA effect size f:", f, "\n\n")

# Non-centrality parameter
# λ = f * sqrt(N)
lambda <- f * sqrt(N)
cat("Non-centrality parameter (λ = f√N):", lambda, "\n\n")

# Degrees of freedom
df1 <- k - 1  # numerator df (between groups)
df2 <- N - k  # denominator df (within groups)
cat("Degrees of freedom:\n")
cat("  Numerator (between groups):", df1, "\n")
cat("  Denominator (within groups):", df2, "\n\n")

# Critical value from central F distribution
F_crit <- qf(p = 1 - alpha, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = 0)
cat("Critical F-value at α =", alpha, ":", F_crit, "\n\n")

# Power: Pr(F > F_crit | H1 is true)
# Using non-central F distribution with non-centrality λ
power <- 1 - pf(q = F_crit, df1 = df1, df2 = df2, ncp = lambda)

cat("Power (Pr(reject H0 | H1 true)):", power, "\n\n")

# Report results
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = round(power, 15),
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("Results:\n")
print(results)

# Output in required format
library(jsonlite)
output <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
  )
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(output, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")
